behavior: Closed later include/eval units compile direct CV-assignment anonymous class sites with their actual unit origins, source files and request-wide name suffix. A chronological successful-compilation prefix starting at unit0 supplies the seed; fresh canonical AST occurrences count admitted class sites, never runtime visits or source-unit numbers.

Repeated execution of one compiled site allocates distinct objects of the same class with independent property storage and the same lexical class identity. Recompiling identical include/eval bytes creates the next class name, retaining its raw NUL, actual filename/start line and hexadecimal suffix. include_once skips preserve source, journal, class, code and file images.

Runtime admission checks the installed source descriptor and historical seed for the actual unit; older compiled classes remain valid after later compilations. Existing unit0/factory rules remain literal. No parser, response schema, task or machine-field change is introduced.
engine_routes: Zend/zend_compile.c::zend_generate_anon_class_name uses CG(rtd_key_counter)++; zend_compile_class_decl retries names already present. zend_build_runtime_definition_key also consumes class RTD keys for deferred named declarations.
Zend/zend_vm_def.h::ZEND_DECLARE_ANON_CLASS caches the compiled site class, separating repeated runtime allocation from fresh compilation identity.

Zend/zend_compile.c::zend_compile_short_circuiting can omit a constant-dead expression RHS. The new source certificate therefore requires an actual assignment statement to a literal CV, excluding skipped-expression sites. Statement-body compilation remains distinct from runtime reachability.

Existing module383 unit0/factory compilation and runtime allocation are reused. Named function, Closure and arrow source shapes are conservatively excluded from this dynamic-history slice; they are not claimed to consume this class-name counter.
